claims.claim: Cyril of Alexandria was bishop of Alexandria from 412 until his death in 444.
Cyril was born c. 375 and died June 27, 444.
Cyril succeeded his uncle Theophilus as bishop of Alexandria in 412.
Cyril was named a doctor of the church in 1882.
The work 'Fragmenta in Acta apostolorum et in epistulas catholicas' survives in Greek manuscript form, including MS Α. VI. 17 at the Monastery of El Escorial.
The fragments include commentary on the Acts of the Apostles and the Catholic Epistles, including the Epistle of James.
Cyril is chiefly known for his campaign against Nestorius, bishop of Constantinople, whose views on Christ's nature were declared heretical.
Cyril was one of the two most influential episcopal leaders of Alexandria during Late Antiquity, second only to Athanasius.
